ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF TRENGGALEK REGENCY
NUMBER 10 OF 2012
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL
The existence of Regional Regulations that favor vulnerable or subordinated groups, particularly women and children, has become very necessary in connection with the many social problems that result in the deprivation of human rights of women and children.

The human rights of women and children are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child as well as the ratification of the convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, however the enforcement of human rights of women and children still cannot encourage them to become a political commitment in the Region.

The form of implementation of protection for women carried out by the Government is to implement gender mainstreaming, which is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of Regional development program policies within the framework of National development.

Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

- 40 - Although Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection has included the rights of children, the implementation of obligations and responsibilities of parents, family, community, government, and the state to provide protection to children, a Regional Regulation is still needed as a juridical basis for the implementation of these obligations and responsibilities in the Region. Thus, the formation of this Regional Regulation is based on the consideration that child protection in all its aspects is part of development activities in the Region, particularly in advancing national and state life.

Parents, family, and community are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the state and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development optimally and in a directed manner.

This Regional Regulation affirms that the accountability of parents, family, community, Regional Government and the state is a series of activities carried out continuously for the protection of children's rights. This series of activities must be sustainable and directed to ensure the growth and development of children, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially. This action is intended to realize the best life for children who are expected to be potential successors to the nation, resilient, having nationalism imbued with noble character and Pancasila values, and having a strong will to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state.

Child protection efforts need to be implemented as early as possible, namely from the fetus in the womb until the child is 18 (eighteen) years old. Starting from the concept of holistic, comprehensive, and complete child protection, this Regional Regulation places the obligation to provide protection to children based on the following principles:
a. non-discrimination;
b. the best interests of the child;
c. the right to life, survival, and development; and d. respect for the views of the child.

- 41 - In conducting guidance, development and protection of children, the role of the community is needed, whether through child protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions.

The form of implementation of child protection carried out by the Regional Government is through mainstreaming children's rights, namely integrating children's issues and rights into every stage of development which includes planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of legislation, policy programs, activities and budgets with the principles of the best interests of the child.

The integrity and harmony of a happy, safe, peaceful and tranquil household is the aspiration of everyone in the household. The Republic of Indonesia is a state based on Belief in the One and Only God as guaranteed by Article 29 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Thus, every person within the household scope in exercising their rights and obligations must be based on religion. This needs to be continuously developed in order to build household integrity.

To realize this integrity and harmony, it is very dependent on each person within the household scope, especially the quality level of behavior and self-control of each person within the household scope.

The integrity and harmony of the household can be disrupted if quality and self-control cannot be controlled, which ultimately can lead to domestic violence resulting in insecurity or injustice towards people within the household scope.

To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of domestic violence, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the Pancasila philosophy and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state views that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination. The state's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with - 42 - its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something that is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and household neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate domestic violence.

The Regional Regulation regulates matters of prevention and protection as well as recovery for victims of violence, and regulates matters of obligations for law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer companions, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive to household interests which from the outset are directed towards household integrity and harmony. To carry out prevention of domestic violence, the Regional Government is obliged to carry out tasks in the field of women's empowerment to implement preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education about the prevention of violence against women and children.

Based on this thinking, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation that is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly in the implementation of protection for women and children including protection for women and children victims of violence.
